newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks close higher on electricity stocks.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks close higher on electricity stocks.

text.p: Chile's bolsa closed modestly higher Wednesday, driven by energy sector stocks which rebounded on much-awaited rainfall in central and southern parts of the country, dealers said.

"Electricity stocks were battered by a long drought, and although we're still far from being able to say the dry spell is over, at least these rains have improved conditions in several hydro-electric dams," one trader said.
The blue-chip IPSA index .IPSA added 0.6 percent to 117.94, while the broad market shed 0.2 percent. Volume picked up to 11.9 billion pesos from Tuesday's weak tally of 7.5 billion.
Traders said the market was driven by local players who shrugged off Wall Street's pullback following the dramatic rise seen Tuesday in New York.

The day's standout was electricity stock Colbun, which jumped 2.9 percent to 35 pesos. Colburn was severely affected by the drought but benefitted from heavy rainfall Wednesday in areas where its dams are located.
Weakest performers included cement stocks, hurt by news mining company Soquimich would join the industry.
Traders said the market was likely to open rangebound Wednesday, with investors keeping close tabs on the weather.
